findings.claim: A clip's Loading Type (clip metadata v6 LoadMode byte) is 0 = always in memory, 1 = load on demand with a resident short piece, 2 = load on demand. For types 1 and 2 the engine takes a reader count on the clip for every bone it samples (a LOCK CMPXCHG that all sampling workers contend on) and blocks the sampling worker until the data has loaded. Type 0 does neither. DualWield had all 293 clips at type 2: 500 against 500 dual wielders cost 8.3 s of CPU in 45 s, and 0.14 s once every clip was resident.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge src/MithrilForge.Anim/ClipLoading.cs:7-21 (cites docs/perf-audit/clip-reader-lock.md, which is not on any pushed branch); docs/engine/modding-kit.md:543-544 (v6 load mode byte 0/1/2) and :783-788 (resident-clip feature built on feat/perf-audit); bannerlord commit db97bc5e message (8.3 s vs 0.14 s, 'their profile, 02.10.'; 293 always in memory; seen on foot only, rider clips untried); bannerlord HoN/DualWield/README.md:31 ('stay in memory instead of loading in the middle of a battle').
findings.why: TAOM's own battle clips sit at type 2: 24 of the 30 bound hill-troll release/blocked clips and the elephant's 8 attack clips. Every troll on the field would pay the per-bone lock each frame, and the first play of a clip stalls a worker (a first-use hitch). TAOM records the Loading Type semantics and leaves open 'where a Loading Type 2 clip's keyframes come from', but has nothing on the lock or its CPU cost. TAOM's loose-tree clips carry no cooked segment, and the kit writes cooked clips into RuntimeDataCache (modding-kit.md:916-918), so an on-demand load probably means an RDC read mid-battle [inferred].
findings.candidateLever: Take a Loading Type census over the TAOM and Armory clips bound to battle actions. Set 0 where the clip's (SourceAnimation, source window) key is unique (see E1-02), then A/B a troll-heavy Custom Battle on [MissionPerf] avgMs and p95Ms.

findings.claim: For Loading Type 0 the engine shares resident clip data through a cache keyed by the clip's SourceAnimation guid plus its source window. A clip cloned from a template that keeps the template's guid and window is handed the template's data ('the thrust stays a right-hand attack', 11.09). A resident clone therefore needs a data key of its own. MithrilForge derives one from the clip name; the guid need not name an existing animation, because the client's clip loader uses it only as a null check and as the cache key. This also reconciles anim-findings' older reading ('UnknownUInt2 == 2 plays the clip's own segment, 0 plays the referenced animation').
findings.evidence: MithrilForge src/MithrilForge.Anim/ClipLoading.cs:16-27 and :42-57; docs/engine/modding-kit.md:783-788 (resident build is clip-for-clip the in-game-confirmed package, 293/293); docs/anim-findings.md:30-33; bannerlord commit db97bc5e message ('Type 0 alone would hand our clips the vanilla data ... so each clip gets a key derived from its name').
findings.why: TAOM's guides tell modders to set Loading Type 0 on any bound clip, with no cache-key caveat. For clips cloned or repointed from vanilla or Armory templates (set_clip_balance_name.py, repoint_anim_clip.py, generated troll and animalia clips) that advice could silently swap the motion to the template's. TAOM's adopt review still lists this mechanism as 'a possible reconciliation, unverified'.
findings.candidateLever: Before setting any TAOM clip to 0, check that its (SourceAnimation guid, Source1..Source2) pair is unique across the loaded packages, and add that check to the clip checker.

findings.claim: The kit ties Loading Type 1 to a 'Shortened optimized animation' segment (8fc3fc2a), present on 1,944 of 6,177 shipped clips. The kit refuses type 1 for clips of 3.0 s or less and for reversed clips. yotthani's assumption: the shortened payload is the part kept resident while the full clip streams in. 563 shipped clips use type 1, and clip metadata v5 has no form for it.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:920-929 (refusal string, 1,944/6,177, v1-layout shortened payload, the explicit assumption) and :795-799 (563 clips at type 1, no v5 form).
findings.why: TAOM records the kit's 3.0 s warning and the 563-clip census, not the shortened segment or what it is for. A TAOM tool that rewrites clip metadata or flips types should not copy or drop 8fc3fc2a blindly, and type 1 on long creature clips keeps only a short head resident.

findings.claim: The trailing i32 of an optimized-animation (6c1e136f) segment is the clip's in-memory allocation size (size_in_bytes, formula given), matching on 6,177 of 6,177 shipped clips. A wrong value is the likeliest cause of the 'rglBuffer::read_void overrun' crash. The kit's encoder sets key counts and bit widths from a per-bone error budget (0.01 m / family count; 20 % quantisation, 80 % key reduction), which is what decides clip size.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:1033-1052 (formula, assert, 6,177/6,177 round trip) and :948-978 (encoder policy, read from Ghidra, not yet checked against data).
findings.why: It would let TAOM estimate resident clip memory offline for its registration surface (37,708 actions and 1,260 action sets) [inferred]. Not a frame-time lever. TAOM already records the overrun crash.

findings.claim: MBAPI.IMBAgent.GetMaximumNumberOfAgents() compiles to MOV EAX,0x7F8 (2040); the 1.5.3 getter is at 0x1806e4fa0. The cap is baked into Mission's memory layout: two embedded Agent[2040] pools (~6.3 MB each, stride 0xC60) with 16-bit free lists. The '32760' some mods advertise is 32768−8, a short index, not a supported count. About 40 constants in ~16 functions and ~1000 fixed offsets in ~150 functions depend on the pools. Verdict: do not patch.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/native.md:63-76. Corroboration: TAOM's E:/ghidra/TAOM/Win64_Shipping_Client-45be32c57c451f78.engine-methods.json maps get_maximum_number_of_agents to 7229344 = 0x6E4FA0. It is the same client binary (hash 45be32c5, which yotthani cites at modding-kit.md:30), but the instruction body was not decompiled here.
findings.why: This is the hard ceiling for TAOM's big creature battles. Every mount (horse, warg, elk, mumak) and every corpse holds a slot. TAOM's docs only use MaxNumberOfAgentsForMission − NumberOfAgents (mount-despawn).
findings.candidateLever: Record the cap in docs/reference/engine. Any TAOM battle-size or reinforcement lever must keep soldiers plus mounts under 2040.

findings.claim: Three layers sit between the menu and the native cap. (1) BannerlordConfig._battleSizes = {200,300,400,500,600,800,1000}; BattleSize is an index 0–6, and 7 is discarded. (2) Per mission, _battleSize = Min(real, MaxNumberOfAgentsForMission/2), because a mounted agent takes two slots and riderless horses are agents too. (3) The native 2040. Raising the limit means reflection on _battleSizes[6] plus lifting the /2 cap, and the mod must then keep soldiers plus horses under the native maximum or the mission crashes. The practical ceiling is about 1000 simultaneous agents with horses; more combatants means reinforcement waves.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/combat.md:107-127. Re-checked in the local v1.5.3 decompile: E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/_categories_v1.5.3/MountAndBlade/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade/BannerlordConfig.cs:60; DefaultBattleMissionAgentSpawnLogic.cs:47-60 (cache, then MaxNumberOfTroopsForMission => MaxNumberOfAgentsForMission / 2) and :121 (Min).
findings.why: Mounted creatures (warg riders, elk, the mumakil crew) spend two slots per combatant, so TAOM's effective field is smaller than the slider suggests. Any TAOM battle-size option must respect both the /2 rule and 2040.
findings.candidateLever: Document the layers next to mount-despawn. Gate any battle-size override with a soldiers+mounts ≤ 2040 check.

findings.claim: About 1000 agents run at 19–21 FPS on yotthani's reference machine, and the bottleneck is the vanilla engine, not a mod. DualWield's dated measurements point the same way: 41–48 fps with 936 dual wielders on the field; a dense battle fell to 34 fps on its own while DualWield's strikes took 0.5–3 % of the frame; 997 dual wielders cost 138–148 ms/s in the strike sweep at 34 fps before the cuts.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/combat.md:127-129 (no date or log given for the 19–21 FPS line); bannerlord HoN/DualWield/Core/DwPerf.cs:7-9; bannerlord commits 9303377f and 4fb27d32 (messages).
findings.why: A baseline for reading TAOM's [MissionPerf] numbers: big battles are engine-bound before TAOM code costs anything, so TAOM perf work should report its own share of the frame, not total fps. TAOM already cites the 936-dual-wielder call counts.

findings.claim: Mission.GetNearbyAgents(center, radius, list) returns active humans only: no mounts, ridden or riderless, and no agents that are no longer active (killed, unconscious). A list-based cast must add the riders' mounts itself (agent.MountAgent). Measured over 113,601 + 143,038 rays in two big battles.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/combat.md:142-146 (added 117b04fc, 2026-10-02); bannerlord commit 29795cc7 message. Caveat: the doc's own counts attribute only 342 of 357 and 439 of 472 misses to fallen bodies and mounts. It also contradicts yotthani's earlier taom-combat.md:332 ('GetNearbyAgents; includes mounts/horses').
findings.why: Several TAOM creature features call GetNearbyAgents: the elephant/mumakil/war-ram trample (ElephantLikeAttackTasks.cs:59), its engage gate (ElephantLikeEngageDecorator.cs:52), the troll's BruteForceReadyDecorator.cs:48 and SmartCavalryAIMissionBehavior.cs:110. TAOM's war-ram log already showed the butt hitting mounted lords 'and never their horses'. Yet ElephantLikeAttackTasks.cs:72-75 still guards against mounts as if they could arrive [inferred dead code], and the trample can never hit horses [inferred].
findings.candidateLever: Decide per feature whether mounts should be hit or avoided. Where yes, add MountAgent explicitly, as DualWield did in 29795cc7. Fix the misleading comment.

findings.claim: Mission.RayCastForClosestAgentsLimbs walks every agent: 65–70 µs per call with 1,600 agents (later measured at ~78 µs). It tests the limbs of ONE agent, the one with the nearest origin among those whose box the ray touches, and reports nothing if that agent's capsules are missed, even when another body further along is cut. DualWield's one-agent ray calls the native capsule builder (RVA 0x681240) and capsule test (RVA 0x5c61b0) directly. Each RVA is checked against 28 bytes (unique in the file), and the code falls back to the engine ray on any build other than 1.5.3. Results: 1.17–1.28 µs per cast; a pre-filter (men within 2 m of the ray, mounts within 3 m) brings it to 7.7 casts per ray instead of 28; about 4 ms/s for all rays. Strike outcomes are unchanged (16.6/28.9/36.5 % vs 16.1/29.5/37.4 %), and bone and distance are identical on 5,275 + 4,625 shared hits. RayCastForGivenAgentsLimbs returns a bone index the hit code rejects, which raises an access violation in the damage call.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/combat.md:147-159; bannerlord commits 6bf89e75 (~78 µs, the RVAs, 28-byte check), 29795cc7 (pre-filter, 28 casts before), e0186626 (~4 ms/s, Live by default; README.md patch at :173-175), 41016773 and ef4cdece (65–70 µs), 7688029a (Given-agents AV, reverted), c8f5973c (4 rays 31–36 ms/s vs 2 rays 14 ms/s and −16 % hits). The nearest-origin mechanism cites the missing docs/perf-audit/limb-ray-given-agent.md.
findings.why: TAOM records the 65–70 µs cost and the Given-agents AV trap, not the one-agent semantics or the native path. TAOM's creature code casts no limb rays today (grep: no RayCastFor* in Main), but scripted-melee-strikes.md §9 lists 'limb rays for creature contact' as an option, and the per-call cost scales with agent count. TAOM's client Ghidra project is the same binary, so the two RVAs can be checked there.
findings.candidateLever: If creature contact moves to limb rays, budget about 70–80 µs per call at 1,600 agents. Verify 0x681240 and 0x5c61b0 with tools/native_decompile.py --rva before considering a native-pointer path.

findings.claim: Vanilla refreshes each AI agent's formation values on a ~0.45–0.55 s timer inside the parallel agent tick (Agent.TickParallel → ParallelUpdateCachedAndFormationValuesForAIAgent → HumanAIComponent.ParallelUpdateFormationMovement), plus a native SetFormationInfo about every 0.5 s. A mod loop over 1000+ agents every frame is therefore unnecessary: stagger per formation every 0.3–0.5 s and reuse MBList buffers (RBM uses [ThreadStatic] lists). Rank indices churn (SwitchFrontUnitTypesToFrontRows about every 0.5 s), so re-read them rather than cache. SetScriptedPosition per agent is 'expensive and jerky' [yotthani's assumption].
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/ai-formations.md:28, :31, :37, :78, :100, :102 (German; translated). Re-checked in v1.5.3 Agent.cs:1626: new Timer(Mission.CurrentTime, 0.45f + MBRandom.RandomFloat * 0.1f).
findings.why: The cadence guide for TAOM's per-agent logic (SmartCavalryAI, MixedFormations, creature behaviour trees). TAOM already notes the 0.45–0.55 s timer, the 0.5 s FormationAI tick and uses scratch buffers.

findings.area: AI behaviour values / native sync cost
findings.claim: OverrideBehaviorParams (and the extension Agent.SetAIBehaviorValues) only marks _hasNewBehaviorValues. SyncBehaviorParamsIfNecessary in OnTickParallel then pushes the values natively (SetAllAIBehaviorParams). Every call re-marks the set dirty, so set values only when the agent's state changes. Engine RefreshBehaviorValues (order change, arrangement change, joining a formation) overwrites the override, so it must be re-applied periodically. The direct Agent.SetAIBehaviorParams path bypasses the cache and is overwritten at the next sync.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/ai-formations.md:53-54, :74, :100. Re-checked in v1.5.3: AgentComponentExtensions.cs:55-58 (SetAIBehaviorValues extension calls OverrideBehaviorParams) and HumanAIComponent.cs:144-170, :206.
findings.why: TAOM's howdah and mumakil crews already re-assert every 0.5 s for exactly this reason. One TAOM doc is wrong: analysis-battle-ai-2026-09-17.md:684-685 says no Agent.SetAIBehaviorValues exists and names an AgentComponentExtensions.OverrideBehaviorParams extension. In 1.5.3 the extension is SetAIBehaviorValues, and OverrideBehaviorParams is a HumanAIComponent instance method.

findings.claim: Formation.GetOrderPositionOfUnit is called on worker threads of the parallel agent tick (via Agent.GetBaseFormationFrame), and Formation.SetMovementOrder runs in the asynchronous team tick for AI orders. A prefix there may only read state prepared on the main thread (swap immutable snapshots), must not allocate much, log or touch UI, and should use the ...MT variants.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/hooks.md:109-114 (Conversion/1.5.3, BattleAI MixedFormations stage 1).
findings.why: TAOM verified this independently (#595) and has a mandatory thread table for patches.

findings.area: safety / stat model during agent build
findings.claim: A lesson yotthani took from RBM's commit messages: a stat calculation that called GetNearbyEnemyAgents during Agent.Build deadlocked natively with the parallel formation job at the last reinforcement wave. The engine hung with no exception and no dump. Rule: the stats model does pure arithmetic only, makes no mission queries and never touches agents that are still being built.
findings.evidence: bannerlord docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-armory-design.md:298-302 (German; translated). It cites RBM commits 9b7a3cd, 5e46303, e648fc1 and d4ab486, lessons only, not reproduced by yotthani.
findings.why: A hang with no dump is TAOM's costliest crash class. TAOM's two stat models (TaomAgentStatCalculateModel, TaomCustomBattleAgentStatCalculateModel) contain no GetNearby* or agent-list call (grep). The services they call (ICareerAgentStatService.ApplyAgentStatModifiers) were not traced.
findings.candidateLever: Add a rule to .claude/rules/gamemodels.md and a deep-review grep gate: nothing reachable from AgentStatCalculateModel may query the Mission or its agent lists.

findings.claim: A second RBM lesson: refreshing stats every tick is too expensive. Refresh on events instead (when a driver drifts by 5 % or more), never within 1 s of an agent's creation, and apply the refresh from a buffer after the pass over the agent list. yotthani's hooks.md calls AgentStatCalculateModel the hook point 'for anything computed from agent state every tick', with Agent.UpdateAgentProperties() as the re-trigger.
findings.evidence: bannerlord docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-armory-design.md:303-304; MithrilForge docs/engine/hooks.md:29-31.
findings.why: TAOM's reference says UpdateAgentStats recomputes on a state change while native reads the driven properties every tick. TAOM's area abilities and perks call UpdateAgentProperties on every ally in a radius and on their mounts (MissionAbilityExecutionContext.cs:126-163, CareerPerkMissionBehavior.cs:186-187). There is no rule against bursts or calls right after spawn.

findings.claim: The campaign-map shader variants pbr_main_map_gbuffer and pbr_main_map_shadowmap are not in the shipped shader sack (rgl_log shows 'Missing shader from sack'). The engine compiles them on first use into ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/Shaders/CoreShaders, a cache that a game update empties. Until the compile is stored the prop is simply not drawn, which can last a whole first session with nothing wrong in the package.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:767-772 (in-game, 2026-10-02).
findings.why: TAOM knows about on-demand shader compiles and cache invalidation for battles (its pre-compile walk, parked 2026-09-25, visits battle scenes only) and logs sack misses during battle loads. It has nothing on map-shader variants (grep pbr_main_map: 0 hits). After an engine bump, TAOM_Map and camp/POI props could be invisible in a player's first session, which looks like a package bug.
findings.candidateLever: Have MapLoadDiagnostics count 'Missing shader from sack' lines that name map shaders. Mention first-session map-prop invisibility in post-bump release notes.

findings.area: VRAM / kit texture format and mips
findings.claim: The kit picks the compressed format from the texture name's suffix: _atlas → BC7; _d, _s and anything else → DXT1, or DXT5 with alpha; _n → BC5 (DXT5 with alpha), normalised first and given engine flag 0x80000000; _h → BC4; flag for_skybox_background → BC6H. 'Alpha' means has_alpha set and ignore_alpha not set. Already-compressed sources pass through, and dont_compress skips compression. Mips are generated down to 1×1 (nvtt Kaiser filter, no sRGB round trip); normal-map mips are renormalised, with alpha coverage and optional mip blending.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:136-152 (suffix table, constants at 0x1813b9f28) and :154-159 (mips); :177-180 (the cheap win: DXT1 for opaque albedo, BC5 for normals).
findings.why: Thousands of Armory and TAOM_Map textures go through the kit. A normal map not named _n gets DXT1/DXT5 instead of BC5, so texture naming is a zero-code VRAM and quality lever. TAOM knows the bytes per format and the uncompressed fallback for sizes not divisible by 4, not the suffix rule.
findings.candidateLever: Join the texture format strings that tools/audit_map_scene_memory.py already decodes against each name's suffix; rename or re-import the mismatches.

findings.claim: The engine's texture flag table (0x1812e9780), stored by name, gives: dont_degrade 0x2, dont_compress 0x20, dont_delay_loading 0x80, dont_resize_in_atlas 0x100, is_cubemap 0x2000 (system), has_alpha 0x8000 (system), ignore_alpha 0x80000, for_colorgrade 0x100000, for_terrain 0x200000, is_bumpmap 0x400000, is_specularmap 0x800000, is_envmap 0x1000000, and the for_skybox_* flags. yotthani gives the bits but does not reverse what dont_delay_loading or dont_degrade do.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:161-175.
findings.why: TAOM uses Do Not Compress + Dont Degrade for lossless data maps, and its map audit decodes flag names; dont_delay_loading has 0 hits in TAOM docs. dont_delay_loading is likely an eager-load switch for first-use hitches, and dont_degrade likely exempts a texture from the texture-quality mip drop [both inferred from the names]. Texture quality controls about 2.3 GB of the map's 4.4 GB (TAOM measurement).
findings.candidateLever: Count which TAOM textures carry dont_degrade or dont_delay_loading. Find each flag's consumer with tools/native_decompile.py --string on the client project.

findings.area: residency / module textures are not virtual-textured
findings.claim: On a client publish the kit hands a texture to the Granite tiler only if it is 2D, power-of-two in both sides, depth 1 and array 1 (tile 512, or 1024 for for_terrain). It first loads GraniteScripts/BannerlordIgnoredResourceFiles.xml, which the kit does not ship. yotthani's assumption: the step therefore fails for modders, and module textures stay ordinary, non-tiled ones. Vanilla textures keep only a raw mip tail (segment 54d56503, 512 px down) in the package, with the large mips in the streaming files. Module textures, and 202 game textures, carry all their pixels in 70ee4e2c; a tiled texture is one with U2 != 0.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:1089-1095 (publish filter, assumption stated), :677-680 (mip tail / streaming files), :851-853 (54d56503 + non-zero Value64 on nearly every game texture); docs/donor-findings.md:162-167.
findings.why: This would explain why TAOM_Map's 2.34 GB of textures never get vanilla-style streaming: every module texture ships as a full mip chain. TAOM's VMMap pass already shows whole chains held in system memory, so dimensions and compression are the levers left.
findings.candidateLever: Cap module texture dimensions and max mip count, and BC-compress everything that is not a data map.

findings.claim: Metamesh metadata v1 carries a 'Visible Distance' (kit default FLT_MAX). Shipped small props use 20–50 m (lib_quill_pen 20, kitchen_bowl_fish 30, clay_pot_stew 40), baskets 100–200, and 88 of 230 map_icon_parts use 200. yotthani's advice: a scene prop should pick a distance by its size rather than keep FLT_MAX.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:18, :562-563, :1064-1069 (the editor's first field after Resource File, 0x180eb4020, plus the shipped data).
findings.why: Kit imports default to FLT_MAX, so TAOM_Map and kitbash scene props are likely drawn at every range [inferred]. TAOM audits LOD0-only meshes but never visible distance (grep: 0 hits). The runtime culling effect has not been tested in game by either side.
findings.candidateLever: Count visible distance over TAOM_Map and TAOM metameshes (the MetameshMetadata field) and set distances on small props.

findings.claim: A particle system stores 1–4 LOD start distances (e.g. 0, 30, 60), and every emitter names its LOD. Each emitter's min and max config bound the Particle Detail option (0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High, −1 no bound): the engine creates an emitter only if (min == −1 || min <= level) && (max == −1 || level <= max). The level is the system's own value if set, otherwise the particle_detail graphics option. Two shipped emitters have the pair inverted and are never created. 154 of 678 systems also carry a 512×512 BGRA8 thumbnail (about 1 MB each before compression) that the game does not need.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:372-382 and :446-461 (added 4e6c1b6e, 2026-10-02).
findings.why: No particle-named files exist in the ModuleData or top-level AssetPackages of TAOM, LOTRLOME_Armory or TAOM_Map (checked with find -maxdepth). This only matters if TAOM authors effects.
findings.candidateLever: If TAOM ever ships effects, give heavy emitters a min config of 1 or 2 so Low/Medium Particle Detail drops them, and strip the thumbnails.

findings.area: memory / mesh edit data in shipped packages
findings.claim: Publishing does not strip MeshEditData or EditmodeMiscData from meshes: shipped game packages carry them next to the vertex streams. The segment 'kind' u32 is the data version (0 source/edit data, 1 vertex stream, 2 optimized animation, 3 physics cook, 4 import settings). The vertex stream bb1df897 is what the game renders, and it rebuilds bit-for-bit from the edit data. yotthani does not say whether edit data is resident at runtime.
findings.why: TAOM's map memory audit splits TAOM_Map meshes into 1.02 GB of editor segments against 735 MB runtime ('which is resident is UNKNOWN') and flags edoras_t3's 362 MB of editor geometry. Vanilla ships edit data too, so this is not a TAOM packaging error; the kind tag offers a clean split for the residency question.
findings.candidateLever: Split the map memory manifest by segment kind, then measure one heavy mesh (edoras_t3) with and without its edit data [inferred method].

findings.claim: The kit reorders a mesh's index buffer before writing it (0x18052f190 / 0x18052fe80), a vertex-cache style optimisation; the triangles and their winding stay the same. Meshes written by hand skip this step.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:640-645.
findings.why: Applies only to TAOM's hand-built tpacs (tpac_clone_metamesh.py, MithrilForge camp props). The camp props do not render today, per TAOM's own adopt review.

findings.claim: The client never cooks physics shapes that come from packages: each gets flag +0xb1 and reads its stored static and dynamic cook data. Runtime PhysX cooking runs only for shapes built in code. Convex dynamic cook data stores 8 mirror variants per mesh, chosen by the signs of the entity's scale.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:1131-1135 and :1150-1164 (client 0x180362f30).
findings.why: TAOM's shipped bo_ bodies cost no cooking at load. Any TAOM code that builds physics shapes at runtime would pay PhysX cooking [inferred].

findings.claim: The client reads RuntimeDataCache through a reader at 0x1804849d0 (magic RDC0, version 0). On yotthani's 'first look', an entry names its owner item, the segment type, offsets and sizes, plus the source-file and import-settings checksums, and stays valid while neither changes (validate_rdc 0x180436280, kit editor). The client contains none of the XXH64 prime constants, so it cannot recompute item or segment checksums: checksum=0 loads, and a checksum can matter only as a stored key.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:884-904 (RDC entry layout explicitly 'assumption beyond the bytes shown'); README.md:150-152.
findings.why: TAOM settled by Procmon that the client reads RDC and established it can never rebuild it; TAOM ships 41.1 GB of RDC and keeps item checksum equal to the RDC stamp. yotthani's no-hash finding means RDC load cost is IO, not hashing.

findings.area: load path / loose Assets vs published packs
findings.claim: A kit import writes one small package per source file (Assets/<cat>/x_geo.tpac, x_anm.tpac, x_tex.tpac) holding the import settings, checksums and edit-side data. Cooked data (vertex streams, compressed clips, compiled pixels) goes to RuntimeDataCache/*.rdc, and only a publish packs it into AssetPackages. Publish has three targets: client, dedicated server, editor.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/modding-kit.md:44-60 and :1084-1088.
findings.why: TAOM's three content modules load from loose trees (Armory 4,364 tpacs, TAOM_Map 3,210) plus RDC; loose Assets/ wins even where cooked packs exist. Whether publishing would cut load-time IO is unmeasured by either side [inferred lever].
findings.candidateLever: A/B battle and map load time on a published copy of one module, read off [BattleLoad]/[MapLoad].

findings.area: per-tick engine call cost / hot-path hygiene
findings.claim: DualWield's perf series (2026-09-28/29): per-agent engine calls add up (GetCurrentActionType and FindAgentWithIndex every tick at 936 agents ≈ 45,000 and 56,000 calls/s), fixed by looking at each agent every third tick and sweeping for the dead once a second. ActionIndexCache.Create asks the engine for the name on every call, and GetName() the other way, so resolve once per session and re-ask a −1. A Harmony prefix on Agent.SetActionChannel runs for every action change of every agent, so it must return at once. Formatting log text is costly: about 7,400 per-agent spawn lines at deployment and 28,000 per-hit lines in four minutes. Snapshot a list before iterating it, because kills mutate it.
findings.evidence: bannerlord commits 149e87d8, 716e72ed, 73ddad45, 4fb27d32 (messages); HoN/HeirOfNumenor/CODING_STANDARDS.md:408-430 (reuse collections, throttle OnMissionTick).
findings.why: Already adopted into TAOM's scripted-melee page, and TAOM's diagnostics are toggle-gated.

findings.claim: DualWield caps NPC left strikes by frame rate and by its own share of the frame instead of a fixed number. Every 0.5 s, on fps smoothed over about a second, the cap goes down only when fps < 40 AND the strikes take > 5 % of the frame, and up when fps ≥ 55 or their share < 2 % (range 16–128 from 48). Earlier, a fixed 32 let 40–60 % of the chances lapse at 800 vs 800, and an fps-only cap sat at 16 for minutes in a battle that was slow on its own, costing 3,700 left chances.
findings.evidence: bannerlord commits f17c3040 and 9303377f (messages); HoN/DualWield/Core/DwPerf.cs:27-31 (StrikeCap, MaxConcurrent); HoN/DualWield/README.md:49-50, :56.
findings.why: TAOM records the idea ('budget by frame share, not a fixed cap'), but no TAOM creature behaviour tree or SmartCavalryAI throttles by frame share.
findings.candidateLever: Gate optional per-agent creature work (brute-force scans, AoE scans) on a frame-share budget fed by [MissionPerf].

findings.area: campaign map / nameplates on worker threads
findings.claim: Vanilla updates every settlement nameplate each frame on worker threads (UpdateNameplateAuxMT → UpdateNameplateMT → RefreshDynamicProperties(forceUpdate: false)). The main-thread forceUpdate = true call comes only on rare events (ownership change, resume). An override should therefore do its work only on the forced path, which keeps it off the hot path and off worker threads.
findings.evidence: bannerlord HoN/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-settlement-capital-icons-design.md:26-29. Confirmed locally in E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/_modules_build/SandBox__SandBox.ViewModelCollection.cs:9714-9720 and :10581-10587 (file dated 2026-09-15, same day as the v1.5.3 decompile).
findings.why: TAOM's map carries ~988 settlements (map-load-diagnostics heartbeat sample). TAOM patches only the widget's DetermineTargetAlphaValue (~3000 calls/s); any future TAOM patch on SettlementNameplateVM.RefreshDynamicProperties (culture or relation styles) would run per settlement per frame off the main thread.

findings.claim: 1.5.x rebuilt map visibility: PartyBase.UpdateVisibilityAndInspected no longer exists, and a settlement's visibility is no longer recomputed every tick. It is now a plain flag the game sets on events, the way 1.5.x hides and reveals its own hideouts.
findings.evidence: bannerlord TAOM_POI/RELEASE-NOTES.md:53-56 (v1.3.9, commit 12eed19f, 2026-09-27; compiled against 1.5.3 and 1.4.8).
findings.why: Per-tick campaign visibility cost moved to events in 1.5.x. TAOM features that hide or reveal map objects should set the flag on events rather than poll [inferred]. TAOM mentions the old method only in raw review logs.

findings.claim: In a per-tick map visual, GetPathBetweenAIFaces is the expensive call: throttle it to every 1–2 s per route. Repositioning about 60 pooled arrows per tick is negligible ('the native track manager does 256+').
findings.evidence: bannerlord HoN/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-supply-route-visualization-design.md:132-134 (a design statement, no measurement).
findings.why: TAOM's SupplyLines already caches the nav path and throttles the trail. TaomPartyNavigationModel.cs:159 calls GetPathDistanceBetweenAIFaces inside a GameModel, whose call rate is not measured [inferred watch item].

findings.claim: Texture.CreateTextureFromPath returns null for mod PNGs, so use Texture.LoadTextureFromPath. Texture.CreateFromMemory works but leaks. .NET decompresses a PNG to an uncompressed bitmap in memory, so avoid loading many full-size PNGs (2048×1423) and use bbox-cropped versions.
findings.evidence: bannerlord LOTRAOM_FactionMap/CLAUDE.md:128-129 (commit 522388ec, 2026-02-12).
findings.why: TAOM already found the FactionMap textures loaded and never freed (one PNG decodes to 281 MB) and capped them.

findings.claim: Vanilla map props are frugal (12–487 faces) because hundreds of settlements render at once; about 1000 triangles is fine for a one-off prop. Props that share an atlas store it once (twenty props off one 512² texture ship 1 MB, not 20). MithrilForge writes raw R8G8B8A8_UNORM textures for quality, though DXT1 demonstrably works. A LOD-free donor avoids stale distant LODs, which matters on the campaign map where distant LODs show almost always.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge README.md:53-56, :142-145, :179-183, :192-206; docs/engine/modding-kit.md:177-180.

findings.area: per-tick native IK / bake at equip time
findings.claim: Native IK puts a rider's left hand on the rein after the animation clip, every mission tick (FUN_18066b910). The decision reads only the right-hand weapon's TwoHandIdleOnMount flag (bit 21) in the per-agent stats copy, plus channel-1 weight and the mount/dismount action; the left item is consulted only for HasToBeHeldUp. The monster XML rein_* values are not inputs, and the release fades at 3.0/s. The cheap lever sets the flag on the per-agent copy in a prefix on Agent.WeaponEquipped: baked once at equip time, with the shared ItemObject untouched.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/rider-ik.md:9-30 and :47-60 (Ghidra agentlimit/bl153 plus the [Rider] in-game probe, 2026-10-02).
findings.why: It shows the pattern of baking per-agent weapon data once at equip time instead of working every tick. TAOM documents the rein_* XML fields for its creature mounts, not the native decision; the effect is cosmetic.

findings.claim: The collision data handed to OnMissileHit must be copied, not held by reference: the engine reuses or invalidates it right after the callback returns.
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/hooks.md:39-40 (sourced to memory files, no line citation).
findings.why: TAOM's code overrides no OnMissileHit (grep in Main).

findings.area: cheap hooks / player orders without Harmony
findings.claim: OrderController.OnOrderIssued fires on the main thread after an order has been applied to every selected formation. A click on an enemy formation is a plain Charge followed by SetTargetFormation(target). A mod's own SetMovementOrder calls, the team AI and engine re-sets never fire it. SetControlledByAI(true) fires no event, and every SetMovementOrder ends with SetTargetFormation(null).
findings.evidence: MithrilForge docs/engine/hooks.md:42-69 (OrderController.cs:46, :812-831, :1659; Formation.cs:736, :810-835 in Conversion/1.5.3).
findings.why: TAOM documents the same Charge-then-SetTargetFormation sequence and the null target for its Harmony-based SmartCavalryAI. The event is a Harmony-free alternative for features that only need to see player orders.

findings.claim: From FaceLearner's own analysis: a full AgentVisuals recreation is expensive (it happened on every gender change), and so is a full RefreshCharacter per morph change (skeleton tick, resource check, visibility toggle). Caching bitmaps in memory was rejected because of GDI+ memory leaks in .NET, so file-based image I/O remains.

notes:
The highest-value new items for TAOM are E1-01 and E1-02 (clip residency), E1-08 (GetNearbyAgents), E1-15 (map shaders) and E1-05/E1-06 (agent cap).

**Clip residency (E1-01, E1-02).** Clips at Loading Type 1 or 2 take a per-bone lock and block the sampling worker; 24 of the 30 bound hill-troll release/blocked clips sit at 2. Type 0 shares data by (SourceAnimation guid, source window), so TAOM's own 'set Loading Type 0' advice is unsafe for clips cloned from a template. The lock mechanism rests on an unpushed write-up, so yotthaniStatus is unclear; the type-0 cache key is backed by an in-game observation.

**GetNearbyAgents (E1-08).** It returns no mounts and no fallen agents. This contradicts yotthani's own taom-combat.md:332, and TAOM's ElephantLikeAttackTasks.cs:72-75 still guards against mounts arriving.

**Map shaders (E1-15).** Campaign-map shader variants compile on first use, so a map prop can stay invisible for a whole first session after a game update. TAOM's pre-compile walk covers battles only.

**Agent cap (E1-05, E1-06).** The native cap is 2040, and a mounted agent takes two slots.
